parsed.summary: The main theorem is Theorem 1.1. Let S ⊂ ℝⁿ be convex and compact with nonempty interior and barycenter 0, and suppose the only lattice point in int S is 0. Then the Lebesgue volume of S is at most (n+1)ⁿ/n!. Separate results show that the centered simplex (n+1)Δₙ − 𝟙 has barycenter 0 and volume (n+1)ⁿ/n!, and that some admissible body attains the bound. No substantive caveat was found; the most notable minor point is that the sharpness statement is existential and does not say the extremizer is the simplex.

glossary.plain: Δₙ = {x : xᵢ ≥ 0 for all i, Σxᵢ ≤ 1} = conv{0, e₁, …, eₙ}

glossary.standard_concept: affine map sending Δₙ to the centered simplex

glossary.plain: Lebesgue volume of K as a real number (toReal; 0 if infinite)
glossary.note: The name says 'normalized' but it is ordinary volume, which is what the paper uses. Bodies are compact, so the volume is finite.
Junk value 0 when vol(K) = 0, but every use requires nonempty interior, so the volume is positive.

glossary.plain: int(K) ∩ ℤⁿ, viewed as a set of integer vectors
convex, compact set with nonempty interior, barycenter 0, and int ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}

lean_claims.plain: For every n and every S ⊆ ℝⁿ that is convex, compact, has nonempty interior, has barycenter 0, and satisfies int(S) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}: vol(S) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!.
For every n, the barycenter of (n+1)Δₙ − 𝟙 is 0.
For n > 0, there exists a convex compact body with nonempty interior, barycenter 0 and int ∩ ℤⁿ = {0} whose volume equals (n+1)ⁿ/n!.

paper_claims.plain: Let K ⊂ ℝⁿ be a full-dimensional compact convex body with barycenter 0 and int(K) ∩ ℤⁿ = {0}. Then vol(K) ≤ (n+1)ⁿ/n!.
The simplex (n+1)Δₙ − (1, …, 1) has barycenter 0, has no other interior lattice point, and has volume (n+1)ⁿ/n!.

coverage.why: Hypotheses and conclusion match; hn : 0 ≤ n is vacuous.
Lean asserts only that some extremizer exists. The barycenter and volume of the simplex are proved separately, but no theorem states that the simplex's interior lattice points are exactly {0}.

flags.explanation: The existential statement does not identify the extremizer as the centered simplex. The paper's claim that this simplex has 0 as its only interior lattice point is not stated anywhere. Sharpness of the bound itself is still captured.
The hypothesis hn : 0 ≤ n is vacuous. The n = 0 case is consistent: volume on Fin 0 → ℝ gives the point mass 1, and the bound is 1⁰/0! = 1.
The hypothesis 0 < n is unnecessary but harmless, since the paper's setting has n ≥ 1.
